new_note: *But I say unto you, That whosoever is angry with his brother without a cause shall be in danger of the judgment: and whosoever shall say to his brother, Raca, shall be in danger of the council: but whosoever shall say, Thou fool, shall be in danger of hell fire.* (Matthew 5:22). *For in the presence of my father I spake peaceably to Joseph; and when I had gone out, the spirit of hatred darkened my mind, and stirred up my soul to slay him.* (Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs 100:2). Gad is speaking to his sons about what he did to Joseph. In front of their father he spoke peaceably, and the moment he had gone out hatred darkened his mind and drove his soul toward killing his brother. That is the road Yahusha (Jesus) is describing: the commandment against murder was never only about the hand, because anger at a brother is where the killing begins. He is not setting the Torah aside but reading the commandment down to its root, the same root Gad learned the hard way and warned his children about.
member_note: Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs 100:2 — *the spirit of hatred darkened my mind, and stirred up my soul to slay him.* Gad confesses that hatred began as a darkened mind and ended in a plan to kill, which is the very path Yahusha (Jesus) traces back to anger.
flag: Old citation (Testament of Gad 2:2) was stale; card sits on the right verse, now cited by the live numbering. Old note quoted the previous verse inside the italics; I quote only 100:2.

new_note: *But I say unto you, Love your enemies, bless them that curse you, do good to them that hate you, and pray for them which despitefully use you, and persecute you;* (Matthew 5:44). *Love ye one another from the heart; and if a man sin against thee, speak peaceably to him, and in thy soul hold not guile; and if he repent and confess, forgive him.* (Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs 100:3). Gad does not stop at loving the brother who treats you well. If a man sins against you, speak peaceably to him, keep no guile in your soul, and forgive him when he repents. Yahusha (Jesus) reaches the same place from the other side, telling us to bless those who curse us, do good to those who hate us, and pray for those who persecute us. This is not a teaching set against Moses; the fathers were already handing it to their sons, and Gad hands it down out of what hatred did to Joseph.
member_note: Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs 100:3 — *if a man sin against thee, speak peaceably to him, and in thy soul hold not guile.* Gad tells his sons to answer a brother's wrong with peace and forgiveness, which is the same heart Yahusha (Jesus) asks for toward an enemy.
flag: Old note quoted 'cast forth the poison of hate', which is not in the live 100:3 (the poison language belongs to the next verse, 100:4); I quote only what 100:3 says. Citation moved from stale 'Gad 2:3' to live 100:3.

new_note: *So likewise shall my heavenly Father do also unto you, if ye from your hearts forgive not every one his brother their trespasses.* (Matthew 18:35). *Love ye one another from the heart; and if a man sin against thee, speak peaceably to him, and in thy soul hold not guile; and if he repent and confess, forgive him.* (Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs 100:3). Yahusha (Jesus) closes His warning with the words from your hearts: the Father will deal with us as we deal with a brother we will not forgive. Gad gives his sons the same measure. Love one another from the heart, speak peaceably to a brother who sins against you, and when he repents and confesses, forgive him. Both put the whole matter in the heart, where a brother is either forgiven or kept in the ledger.
member_note: Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs 100:3 — *Love ye one another from the heart.* Gad's call to love from the heart and forgive the repentant brother stands behind the warning that closes Yahusha's (Jesus's) teaching on forgiveness.
flag: Old note cited stale 'Testament of Gad 62:3' and leaned on Matthew 18:15-17 and the unforgiving-servant parable, neither of which is on this card; I kept the one true link (from the heart, forgive the brother) and cited by live numbering.

new_note: *Even so ye also outwardly appear righteous unto men, but within ye are full of hypocrisy and iniquity.* (Matthew 23:28). *But do not ye, my children, wear two faces like unto them, of goodness and of wickedness; but cleave unto goodness only, for Elohim (God) hath His habitation therein, and men desire it.* (Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs 105:1). Yahusha (Jesus) names the double face plainly: outwardly righteous before men, inwardly full of hypocrisy and iniquity. Asher warns his sons against exactly that, to wear one face and not two, and to cleave to goodness only because Elohim (God) makes His habitation there. What Yahusha (Jesus) exposes in the hypocrite, Asher tells his children to refuse before it ever takes root.
member_note: Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs 105:1 — *wear two faces like unto them, of goodness and of wickedness.* Asher charges his sons not to wear two faces, the same split between outside and inside that Yahusha (Jesus) calls hypocrisy.
flag: Stale numbering in old note ('file ch 67', 'Asher 3:1') replaced by live 105:1. Old note's side references to Ezekiel 13 and 1 John 2:3-4 are not on the card and were dropped.

new_note: *Woe unto you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! for ye are like unto whited sepulchres, which indeed appear beautiful outward, but are within full of dead men’s bones, and of all uncleanness.* (Matthew 23:27). *For they that are double-faced are guilty of a twofold sin; 'for they both do the evil thing and they have pleasure in them that do it', following the example of the spirits of deceit, and striving against mankind.* (Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs 108:2). Yahusha (Jesus) calls the hypocrites whited sepulchres, beautiful on the outside and full of death within. Asher gives the same condition its weight: the double-faced are guilty of a twofold sin, because they do the evil thing and also take pleasure in those who do it. The tomb is the picture of the sin Asher counts twice, a clean outside covering what is in fact within.
member_note: Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs 108:2 — *they that are double-faced are guilty of a twofold sin.* Asher says the double-faced carry a twofold sin, and Yahusha (Jesus) paints the same figure as a whited tomb.
flag: Stale numbering in old note ('file ch 69', 'Asher 5:2') replaced by live 108:2.

new_note: *And then shall appear the sign of the Son of Adam in heaven: and then shall all the tribes of the earth mourn, and they shall see the Son of Adam coming in the clouds of heaven with power and great glory.* (Matthew 24:30). *Until the El Elyon (Most High) shall visit the earth, coming Himself [as man, with men eating and drinking], and breaking the head of the dragon in the water. He shall save Yashar'el (Israel) and all the Gentiles [Elohim (God) speaking in the person of man].* (Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs 109:3). Asher has just told his sons that they will sin, be handed to their enemies, and be scattered to the four corners of the earth. Then he says the Most High will visit the earth, coming Himself as man, and will save Yashar'el (Israel) and the Gentiles, who stand right beside the scattered of the verse before. Matthew shows the same one at the end of that road, the sign of the Son of Adam in heaven, all the tribes of the earth mourning, and the Son of Adam coming in the clouds with power and great glory. The one who comes in the person of man is Yahusha (Jesus), the Formed one who walked with Adam's line from the beginning and came in flesh, and the tribes that mourn are the tribes Asher says were scattered.
member_note: Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs 109:3 — *coming Himself [as man, with men eating and drinking], and breaking the head of the dragon in the water.* Asher says the Most High will come to the earth Himself in the person of man, and Matthew shows that coming with the tribes watching.
flag: MOVED to the next verse (109:3): the old note quotes 'Until the Most High shall visit the earth, coming Himself...', which is 109:3, not 109:2. Old citation 'Asher 6:3' was stale. I identify the one who comes in the person of man as Yahusha (Jesus), the Formed one, per the standing nature-of-God rule; please look at that sentence. Old note's heavy jargon and its Matthew 24:38 aside were dropped.

new_note: *And he shall send his angels with a great sound of a trumpet, and they shall gather together his elect from the four winds, from one end of heaven to the other.* (Matthew 24:31). *But Yahuah (Lord) will gather you together in faith through His tender mercy, 'and' for the sake of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.]* (Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs 109:7). The sons of Asher are told they will be scattered until they do not know their own lands, tribe, and tongue. Yet Yahuah (the Lord) will gather them, and the reason given is Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob: the gathering rests on the fathers and on the blood that carries their promise. Matthew has the same gathering in view, with the elect called in from the four winds. The elect there are the scattered seed of the fathers being brought home, and not a company assembled out of any people by confession.
member_note: Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs 109:7 — *Yahuah (Lord) will gather you together in faith through His tender mercy.* Asher promises that Yahuah (the Lord) will gather the scattered sons for the sake of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, and Matthew describes the elect being gathered from the four winds.
flag: Stale 'Asher 6:7' citation replaced by live 109:7. Old note's string of prophet references (Deuteronomy, Isaiah, Jeremiah, Ezekiel, Hosea, Zechariah) and its Genesis references are not quoted on the card and were dropped; the point (gathered for the fathers' sake, paternal blood remnant, not a spiritual category) is kept.

new_note: *And Yahusha (Jesus) said unto them, Verily I say unto you, That ye which have followed me, in the regeneration when the Son of Adam shall sit in the throne of his glory, ye also shall sit upon twelve thrones, judging the twelve tribes of Yashar'el (Israel).* (Matthew 19:28). *There were twelve harts feeding: and the nine were (first) dispersed over all the earth, and likewise also the three.* (Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs 129:2). Joseph sees twelve harts feeding together, and all twelve end up dispersed over the earth, the nine first and the three likewise. The twelve harts read as the twelve tribes, scattered. Yahusha (Jesus) speaks of those same tribes as a whole people sitting under judgment when the Son of Adam takes His throne, with twelve thrones set for judging the twelve tribes of Yashar'el (Israel). A people who are to be judged as twelve tribes must first be gathered as twelve, and Joseph's vision is the scattering that the gathering answers.
member_note: Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs 129:2 — *There were twelve harts feeding: and the nine were (first) dispersed over all the earth.* Joseph's vision of twelve harts dispersed over the earth is the scattering that Yahusha (Jesus) assumes when He speaks of judging the twelve tribes.
flag: Old note said the nine are the ten northern tribes and the three are the southern house. Nine is not ten and three is not two, so I did not carry that identification; I say only what the verse says (twelve dispersed, nine first, then the three). Old citation ('Joseph 15', 'chapter 86') was stale; live 129:2 used.

new_note: *For this is my blood of the new testament, which is shed for many for the remission of sins.* (Matthew 26:28). *In thee shall be fulfilled the prophecy of heaven [concerning the Lamb of Elohim (God), and Saviour of the world], that a blameless one shall be delivered up for lawless men, and a sinless shall die for ungodly men [in the blood of the covenant, for the salvation of the Gentiles and 'of Israel', and shall destroy Beliar and his servants].* (Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs 133:8). Jacob, embracing Joseph, tells him that in him the prophecy of heaven will be fulfilled: a blameless one delivered up for lawless men, a sinless one dying for ungodly men in the blood of the covenant. Yahusha (Jesus) at the table gives that blood its name, shed for many for the remission of sins. The Testament says the salvation is for the Gentiles and for the house of Yashar'el (Israel), and the Gentiles named beside Yashar'el (Israel) are the nations among whom the scattered seed was sent, which is why the news goes out broadly while the sheep who hear are the ones it was always for.
member_note: Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs 133:8 — *a blameless one shall be delivered up for lawless men, and a sinless shall die for ungodly men.* Jacob's word that a sinless one will die for ungodly men in the blood of the covenant is the death Yahusha (Jesus) names at the table.
flag: MOVED to 133:8. The old note quotes 'The blameless one shall be defiled for lawless men...', which is 133:8, not the card's current verse (133:6, Joseph asking his father to pray for his brethren). 133:8 is two verses on, not adjacent to 133:6, so it does not fit the prev/next rule; I moved it anyway because the old note plainly describes it and the Matthew 26:28 link only works there. Another card (1 Peter 3:18) already sits on 133:8. If a non-adjacent move is not permitted, this card needs a different Matthew verse for 133:6 (Matthew 5:44 is already used there). Old citation 'Benjamin 88:31' stale. Live text reads 'delivered up', not 'defiled'. Old note's 'Maccabean period' and its Isaiah 49:6 aside were dropped.

new_note: *For Joseph also besought our father 'that he would pray for his brethren', that 'the Lord' would not impute to them as sin whatever evil they had done unto him.* (Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs 133:6). *But I say unto you, Love your enemies, bless them that curse you, do good to them that hate you, and pray for them which despitefully use you, and persecute you;* (Matthew 5:44). His brothers had done Joseph evil, and Joseph asked their father to pray for them and that Yahuah (the Lord) would not count it to them as sin. That is Matthew 5:44 lived before it was spoken: praying for those who despitefully use you and persecute you. Benjamin hands the story to his sons as proof that loving an enemy can be done, even when the enemy is your own brother.
member_note: Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs 133:6 — *besought our father 'that he would pray for his brethren', that 'the Lord' would not impute to them as sin.* Joseph asked his father to pray for the brothers who wronged him, which is the love of enemies Yahusha (Jesus) later commands.

new_note: *In thee shall be fulfilled the prophecy of heaven [concerning the Lamb of Elohim (God), and Saviour of the world], that a blameless one shall be delivered up for lawless men, and a sinless shall die for ungodly men [in the blood of the covenant, for the salvation of the Gentiles and 'of Israel', and shall destroy Beliar and his servants].* (Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs 133:8). *For Messiah (Christ) also hath once suffered for sins, the just for the unjust, that he might bring us to Elohim (God), being put to death in the flesh, but quickened by the Spirit:* (1 Peter 3:18). Jacob, embracing Joseph, says that in him the prophecy of heaven will be fulfilled: a blameless one delivered up for lawless men and a sinless one dying for ungodly men. Peter says it of the Messiah (Christ), who suffered once for sins, the just for the unjust, so that He might bring us to Elohim (God). The two lines carry the same shape, the righteous one giving himself for those who are not, and the end of it is bringing the lost home to the Father.
member_note: Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs 133:8 — *a blameless one shall be delivered up for lawless men, and a sinless shall die for ungodly men.* Jacob foretells a sinless one dying for ungodly men, and Peter names the Messiah (Christ) as the just one who suffered for the unjust.

new_note: *Greater love hath no man than this, that a man lay down his life for his friends.* (John 15:13). *And him that hath the grace of a good spirit he loveth as his own soul.* (Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs 134:5). Yahusha (Jesus) names the greatest love as laying down one's life for his friends. Benjamin teaches his sons the same love at its starting measure: the man with the grace of a good spirit loves his brother as his own soul. A man who loves another as his own soul has already begun to hold his own life loosely, and the Messiah (Christ) carries that love to its furthest end.
member_note: Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs 134:5 — *him that hath the grace of a good spirit he loveth as his own soul.* Benjamin teaches loving a brother as one's own soul, the measure that John 15:13 carries to laying down one's life.
flag: Old note cited 'DB ch 89 v.5' (stale) and its italic quote ('loveth the righteous as his own soul') is not what the live verse says; I quote the live 134:5.

new_note: *Even as the Son of Adam came not to be ministered unto, but to minister, and to give his life a ransom for many.* (Matthew 20:28). *And He shall ascend from Hades and shall pass from earth into heaven. And I know how lowly He shall be upon earth, and how glorious in heaven.]* (Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs 139:5). Yahusha (Jesus) says of Himself that the Son of Adam came not to be served but to serve, and to give His life a ransom for many. Benjamin, looking ahead, says he knows how lowly He will be upon the earth and how glorious in heaven. The lowliness and the glory belong to one person: the one who takes the servant's place on earth is the one who ascends from Hades into heaven.
member_note: Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs 139:5 — *I know how lowly He shall be upon earth, and how glorious in heaven.* Benjamin foresees the one who will be lowly on earth and glorious in heaven, and Yahusha (Jesus) says the Son of Adam came to serve and give His life.
flag: Stale old citations ('94:5', 'Testament of Benjamin 9') replaced with live 139:5. Old note's Isaiah 53, 1 Enoch 62 and Philippians 2 references are not on the card and were dropped.

new_note: *And Yahusha (Jesus) came and spake unto them, saying, All power is given unto me in heaven and in earth.* (Matthew 28:18). *And He shall ascend from Hades and shall pass from earth into heaven. And I know how lowly He shall be upon earth, and how glorious in heaven.]* (Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs 139:5). Benjamin says the one who comes will ascend from Hades and pass from earth into heaven, lowly on the earth and glorious in heaven. After the cross and the tomb, Yahusha (Jesus) comes to His disciples and says all power is given to Him in heaven and in earth. The word Benjamin gave his sons is the road that ends in that sentence.
member_note: Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs 139:5 — *He shall ascend from Hades and shall pass from earth into heaven.* Benjamin foresees the ascent from Hades into heaven, and Yahusha (Jesus) states the power given Him in heaven and in earth.
flag: Stale old citations ('Ch 7:5', 'TestXII ch 94:5') replaced with live 139:5. This verse is also on the Matthew 20:28 card; the two cards use different halves of the verse. Old note's Psalm and Ephesians references and its internal cross-card note were dropped.

new_note: *Go ye therefore, and teach all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Ruach HaKodesh (Holy Spirit):* (Matthew 28:19). *For all these things they gave us for an inheritance, saying: Keep the commandments of Elohim (God), until Yahuah (Lord) shall reveal His salvation to all Gentiles.* (Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs 140:5). The fathers left their sons the commandments of Elohim (God) as their inheritance, to be kept until Yahuah (the Lord) reveals His salvation to all the Gentiles. When Yahusha (Jesus) says to go and teach all nations, the message goes out broadly because those it is for are scattered among them and are not known by sight. Benjamin's word has the order right: the commandments stay in the hands of the sons, and the salvation goes out to be heard.
member_note: Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs 140:5 — *Keep the commandments of Elohim (God), until Yahuah (Lord) shall reveal His salvation to all Gentiles.* Benjamin's sons are left the commandments until the salvation is revealed to all the Gentiles, and Yahusha (Jesus) sends His own out to every nation.
flag: Stale old citations ('Ch 8:6', 'TestXII ch 95:6') replaced with live 140:5. Old note quoted only 'And shall reveal His salvation to all Gentiles'; I quote the whole live verse, which also carries the commandments, so Torah stands in the note.

new_note: *Then said Yahusha (Jesus) unto them, Be not afraid: go tell my brethren that they go into Galilee, and there shall they see me.* (Matthew 28:10). *Then shall we also rise, each one over our tribe, worshipping the King of heaven, [who appeared upon earth in the form of a man in humility. And as many as believe on Him on the earth shall rejoice with Him].* (Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs 140:7). After His resurrection Yahusha (Jesus) tells the women to carry word to His brethren, and the brethren He means are sons of Yashar'el (Israel). Benjamin pictures that same people rising from the dead, each patriarch over his own tribe, worshipping the King of heaven who appeared on earth in the form of a man. The Testament keeps the tribes by name and by order, and the Messiah (Christ) still calls them brethren.
member_note: Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs 140:7 — *Then shall we also rise, each one over our tribe, worshipping the King of heaven.* Benjamin sees the patriarchs rising each over his tribe to worship the King, and Yahusha (Jesus) after rising calls His own brethren.
flag: Stale old citations ('Ch 8:7', 'TestXII ch 95:7') replaced with live 140:7. Old note's cross-references (Psalm 22, Hebrews 2, Matthew 12 and 25, Revelation 7, Matthew 19:28) and its thread slug are not on the card and were dropped.

new_note: *And Yahusha (Jesus) came and spake unto them, saying, All power is given unto me in heaven and in earth.* (Matthew 28:18). *Then also all men shall rise, some unto glory and some unto shame. And Yahuah (Lord) shall judge Yashar'el (Israel) first, for their unrighteousness; [for when He appeared as Elohim (God) in the flesh to deliver them they believed Him not].* (Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs 140:8). Benjamin says all men shall rise, some to glory and some to shame, and that Yahuah (the Lord) will judge Yashar'el (Israel) first because they did not believe Him when He appeared as Elohim (God) in the flesh. Yahusha (Jesus) says all power is given to Him in heaven and in earth, and a judge needs that power. Judgment beginning with the house of the fathers is the order the Testament lays out, and Yahusha (Jesus) is the one who holds the authority to carry it through.
member_note: Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs 140:8 — *Yahuah (Lord) shall judge Yashar'el (Israel) first, for their unrighteousness.* Benjamin says Yahuah (the Lord) will judge Yashar'el (Israel) first, and Yahusha (Jesus) holds the power in heaven and in earth to do it.
flag: Stale old citations ('Ch 8:8', 'TestXII ch 95:8') replaced with live 140:8. Old note ran into the next verse (140:9, the Gentiles' judgment) and added Daniel 12:2, Acts 17:31, Matthew 25 and 1 Peter 4:17; none are on the card and they were dropped.
